newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares continue to drift lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares continue to drift lower in thin trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares again slipped in weak trade on Wednesday amid liquidity shortage and negative sentiment caused by persisting political uneasiness, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 .XU100 closed eight points, or 0.56 percent lower at 1,427 after moving between 1,415 and 1,452. Non-stop losses totalled 6.85 percent since the market opened on Thursday following a 6-1/2 day holiday.
Trade volume shrank to 9.95 trillion lira from Tuesday's 11.35 trillion.

"Trade was narrow with low volume as the market remained totally indexed to politics. It may keep waiting for (political) developments for some more time," said Huseyin Istanbullu from Meksa securities.
Brokers said firm support expected at the index's 1,420 level was tested in the afternoon following a 0.14 percent drop to 1,433 in the morning. They await fresh support at 1,400 if 1,420 is broken.
Brokers added that hefty corporate tax payments due end-April were another factor hindering cash influx to the bourse.

Turkish opposition plans to form a secularist alliance against Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan faltered as veteran left-wing leader Bulent Ecevit acknowledged on Wednesday that two other opposition leaders had only loosely agreed to the plan.

Erbakan who challenged his critics on Tuesday to elections has come under heavy fire from secularist centres, led by the powerful army, for his reluctance to implement measures recommended by the army to fight rising Islamist zeal.
Generals said at a rare briefing on Tuesday that the biggest threat facing the country was the domestic threat of separatism and fundamentalism rather than any foreign power.

Of the 249 shares traded, falls outdid rises by 128 to 64 and 57 finished steady. The IMKB Industrial eased 0.63 percent to 1,427, the IMKB Services was unchanged at 1,319 and the IMKB Financial edged down 0.51 percent to 1,548.
Actives were led by utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 2,500 lira at 175,000 and largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, down 250 lira at 13,250. They made up 11.8 percent of the total turnover.
